root_cause_label: Insufficient Image Analysis Leading to Generic Procedural Generation
one_sentence_failure_summary: After reading only 7 pixels of the 48MB path-traced image, the agent falsely assumed the image was a sky/cloud scene and spent all remaining steps iterating cosmetic variations of a generic procedural generator that never bore resemblance to the actual rendered scene.
t_err_evidence: Step 2: agent reads only the first 10 lines of the PPM (header + 7 sky-blue pixels via `head -n 10`) and at step 3 immediately infers the image is a 'sky or water scene' and begins writing a sinusoidal procedural generator, acting on an unverified assumption about the image's content without extracting statistical or structural information from the 48MB file.
t_commit_evidence: Step 3: agent writes image.c with a generic sinusoidal color formula based solely on guessing the image is sky-colored; this procedural approach cannot possibly achieve the required 0.99 similarity to a path-traced 3D scene, locking in failure from this point regardless of the cosmetic tuning that follows.
trigger_explanation: The agent read only 7 pixels from the top of the image (all sky-blue, RGB ~159 197 255) and acted on the unverified assumption that the entire 2400x1800 path-traced image was a uniform sky or water scene. It never used statistical analysis, sampling from different regions, or image conversion tools to verify what the image actually depicts, leading to a fundamentally wrong algorithmic strategy.
